final_decision.rationale: Applying blur_gaussian:1 (sigma=1) followed by brightness_darken_gamma_HSV:5 (gamma=3.5) to clean.png reproduces degraded.png pixel-exactly: PSNR=Infinity dB and all 10 content-independent CI metrics are 0.000. Signal chain: initial full_analysis flagged brightness (mean_shift=-81.4, variance_ratio=0.330, clipped_fraction=6.34%, chroma_ratio=0.341) and a non-JPEG smoothing (gm_ratio=0.290, slope_ratio=1.065, block_boundary=0.993). Darkening-family scan rejected V-shift/RGB-shift (hard clipping 16-31% vs target 6.3%) and gamma-RGB (variance 0.44-0.60 vs 0.330); gamma on HSV-V at sev5 matched mean(-80.2)/var(0.341)/clip(6.2%)/chroma(0.346)/uniqG(188). Blur severity scan picked gaussian sigma=1 (gm 0.2915 vs 0.290). Order test: gamma-then-blur gave 38.83 dB, blur-then-gamma gave Infinity -> target order is blur first (ISP-stage brightness semantics, legal per skill order rules). Runner-up alternative brightness_darken_gamma_HSV:5,blur_gaussian:1 (38.83 dB, CI 10/10) not retained as alternative since winner is pixel-exact (gap infinite).

r1_summary.decision_basis: R0 pipeline (blur_gaussian:1 -> brightness_darken_gamma_HSV:5) reproduces ALL 5 support pairs pixel-exactly (PSNR=inf, CI 10/10, all content-independent metrics diff=0.000). For a fully deterministic pipeline this is conclusive: no alternative function or severity can match better, so no candidate change is justified and no R1 training is launched.
